<a id="letter-a"></a>

## A

<a id="a-stability"></a>**A-stability** — The property that a numerical integrator is stable for every decaying mode (Re hλ < 0) at any step size; backward Euler and the trapezoidal rule are A-stable, explicit methods never are. *First defined in* [02-10](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-10-numerical-methods.md). *See also:* [Stiff system](#stiff-system).

<a id="abstraction"></a>**Abstraction** — A simplified description of a system level that exposes a contract (inputs, outputs, assumptions) and hides internal detail, so that the level above can be designed without the detail. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="ac-analysis"></a>**AC analysis** — A simulation of a circuit's small-signal sinusoidal response versus frequency, computed with phasors after linearizing around the operating point. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="accelerated-life-test"></a>**Accelerated life test** — A test at elevated stress (temperature, voltage, humidity) that makes failures occur sooner, with an acceleration model used to translate results to use conditions. *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="accumulation-function"></a>**Accumulation function** — A(x) = ∫_a^x f(t) dt, the running total of f from a fixed start; for a current it is the charge delivered so far. *First defined in* [01-05](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-05-integrals.md).

<a id="activity-factor"></a>**Activity factor** — α, the fraction of clock cycles in which a node makes a 0→1 transition; it scales the dynamic power αCV²f. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="adiabatic-charging"></a>**Adiabatic charging** — Charging a capacitor with a slowly ramped or stepped source so that the voltage across the series resistance stays small, reducing the loss below ½CV² (to CV²/2N for N equal steps). *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="agile-development"></a>**Agile development** — Iterative development in short cycles (sprints) that each deliver working software, with continuous customer feedback and adaptation to changing requirements (Agile Manifesto, 2001). *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md).

<a id="aliasing-programming"></a>**Aliasing (programming)** — Two or more names referring to the same object, so a change made through one is visible through the others; assignment in Python never copies. *First defined in* [05-01](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-01-python-fundamentals.md).

<a id="amdahls-law"></a>**Amdahl's law** — Speedup on N processors is 1/((1 − p) + p/N) when a fraction p of the work parallelizes; as N → ∞ it approaches 1/(1 − p), so the serial fraction caps scaling. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md).

<a id="amortized-cost"></a>**Amortized cost** — The average cost per operation over a worst-case sequence of operations, in which rare expensive steps are paid for by many cheap ones; a doubling array's append is O(1) amortized. *First defined in* [05-08](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-08-data-structures-and-algorithms.md).

<a id="amperes-law"></a>**Ampere's law** — (Ampère's law.) For steady currents, ∮ B · dl = µ₀ I_enc around any closed loop; with symmetry it gives the fields of wires, solenoids (µ₀nI), toroids and coaxial cables (zero outside). *First defined in* [04-06](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-06-magnetic-fields-and-forces.md).

<a id="ampere-hour"></a>**Ampere-hour** — A unit of charge, 1 Ah = 3600 C, used for battery capacity; 1 mAh = 3.6 C. *First defined in* [01-05](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-05-integrals.md).

<a id="angle-argument"></a>**Angle (argument)** — The direction ∠z of a complex number's arrow, measured counterclockwise from the positive real axis; computed with the quadrant-aware atan2(y, x). This curriculum reports principal values in (−180°, 180°]. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="angular-frequency"></a>**Angular frequency** — ω = 2πf, the rate of a sinusoid's phase advance in rad/s, where f is the frequency in hertz. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="antiderivative"></a>**Antiderivative** — A function F with F' = f; any two differ by a constant, written ∫ f dx = F + C. *First defined in* [01-05](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-05-integrals.md).

<a id="apparent-power"></a>**Apparent power** — S = V_rms·I_rms, in volt-amperes; real power is S times the power factor. Wiring and transformers must be sized for S. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md). *See also:* [Power factor](#power-factor).

<a id="arc-length"></a>**Arc length** — The length of a curve, L = ∫√(1 + f'(x)²) dx, built from the element ds = √(dx² + dy²). *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md).

<a id="arithmetic-intensity"></a>**Arithmetic intensity** — Operations performed per byte moved from memory. A workload whose intensity is below a machine's ridge point (peak operations per second ÷ memory bandwidth) is memory-bound; a matrix–vector product has about 1 flop per byte in 16-bit precision. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="arrhenius-model"></a>**Arrhenius model** — A thermally activated rate ∝ exp(−E_a/(kT)); the acceleration factor between temperatures is exp[(E_a/k)(1/T_use − 1/T_stress)], exponential in the often-uncertain activation energy. *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="assertion"></a>**Assertion** — A statement (assert condition) that stops the program if a condition the code relies on is false; used for internal invariants and tests, not for validating input, because python -O removes assertions. *First defined in* [05-04](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-04-reproducible-workflows.md).

<a id="asymptote"></a>**Asymptote** — A line that a curve approaches in a limit, horizontal (x → ∞), vertical (f → ±∞ at a finite x) or slanted; Bode-plot straight lines are asymptotes of a frequency response. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md).

<a id="autocorrelation-function"></a>**Autocorrelation function** — R_X(t₁, t₂) = E[X(t₁)X(t₂)]; for a stationary process R_X(τ), whose value at τ = 0 is the average power and whose decay measures how long the process remembers. *First defined in* [03-06](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-06-random-processes-preview.md).

<a id="average-power"></a>**Average power** — The energy delivered over an interval divided by its length, (1/T)∫p dt; for varying signals it is the average of v·i, not the product of the averages. *First defined in* [06-01](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-01-charge-current-voltage-power.md).

<a id="average-value"></a>**Average value** — (1/(b − a)) ∫_a^b f dx, the height of the rectangle with the same area; over one period it is a signal's DC value. *First defined in* [01-05](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-05-integrals.md).

<a id="letter-b"></a>

## B

<a id="b10-life"></a>**B10 life** — The time by which 10% of a population has failed, α(−ln 0.9)^(1/γ) for a Weibull; percentile lives matter more than MTTF for wear-out. *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="back-emf"></a>**Back-EMF** — The EMF a running motor's rotating coil generates against its supply, proportional to speed; it limits running current, so a stalled motor draws far more current than a spinning one. *First defined in* [04-07](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-07-faraday-lenz-and-inductance.md).

<a id="backside-power-delivery"></a>**Backside power delivery** — Routing a chip's power supply through thick wires on the back of the thinned wafer, freeing front-side wiring for signals and cutting IR drop; Intel ships it as PowerVia on 18A, and TSMC plans it for A16. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="band-gap"></a>**Band gap** — The range of energies with no allowed electron states between the top of the valence band and the bottom of the conduction band, E_g = E_c − E_v (1.12 eV in silicon); it sets intrinsic carrier density, absorption edge and breakdown strength. *First defined in* [04-11](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-11-intro-solid-state-physics.md).

<a id="bandgap-reference"></a>**Bandgap reference** — A circuit that adds a junction voltage (falling about 2 mV/K) to a voltage proportional to absolute temperature so that the temperature coefficients cancel; its output sits near the silicon bandgap, about 1.2 V. *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="base-rate-effect"></a>**Base-rate effect** — Even an accurate test produces mostly false positives when the condition it detects is rare, because its false-positive rate applies to the large unaffected majority. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="basis"></a>**Basis** — A set of independent vectors that spans a subspace; every vector in the subspace is then a unique combination of the basis vectors. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md).

<a id="bathtub-curve"></a>**Bathtub curve** — A curve shaped like a bathtub, used in two senses: bit error rate against sampling instant across the unit interval, and failure rate against age (infant mortality, flat mid-life, wear-out). *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md).

<a id="bayes-rule"></a>**Bayes' rule** — P(A | B) = P(A) P(B | A)/P(B), which turns the probability of an observation given a cause into the probability of the cause given the observation. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md). *See also:* [Base-rate effect](#base-rate-effect), [Maximum a posteriori (MAP) detection](#maximum-a-posteriori-map-detection).

<a id="beats"></a>**Beats** — The slow swelling and fading of a sum of two sinusoids of nearly equal frequency, or of an undamped system forced near its natural frequency; the envelope varies at half the difference frequency. *First defined in* [02-04](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-04-forced-response-and-resonance.md).

<a id="bernoulli-equation"></a>**Bernoulli equation** — y' + p(t)y = q(t)yⁿ, made linear by the substitution v = y^(1−n); the logistic equation is the case n = 2. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="bias"></a>**Bias** — The difference between an estimator's expected value and the true parameter; mean square error equals bias squared plus variance. *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="big-o-notation"></a>**Big-O notation** — f(n) = O(g(n)) means f grows no faster than a constant multiple of g for large n; it keeps an algorithm's growth rate (constant, log n, n, n log n, n squared) and drops constant factors. *First defined in* [05-08](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-08-data-structures-and-algorithms.md).

<a id="binary-heap"></a>**Binary heap** — A complete binary tree stored in an array (children of i at 2i + 1 and 2i + 2) with every parent no larger than its children; supports a priority queue with O(log n) insertion and removal of the minimum. *First defined in* [05-08](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-08-data-structures-and-algorithms.md).

<a id="binary-search"></a>**Binary search** — Searching a sorted array by comparing with the middle element and discarding half each step; at most floor(log2 n) + 1 comparisons (20 for a million items). *First defined in* [05-08](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-08-data-structures-and-algorithms.md).

<a id="binary-search-tree"></a>**Binary search tree** — A tree whose nodes keep smaller keys in the left subtree and larger keys in the right, so search, insertion and deletion cost O(height); self-balancing variants (red-black, AVL, B-trees) keep the height O(log n). *First defined in* [05-08](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-08-data-structures-and-algorithms.md).

<a id="binomial-distribution"></a>**Binomial distribution** — The number of successes in n independent trials each succeeding with probability p, with PMF C(n,k) p^k (1 − p)^(n − k). *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md).

<a id="binomial-series"></a>**Binomial series** — (1 + x)^α = 1 + αx + α(α − 1)x²/2! + …, valid for |x| < 1 and any real α; the source of (1 + x)^n ≈ 1 + nx. *First defined in* [01-08](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-08-sequences-series-and-taylor.md).

<a id="biot-savart-law"></a>**Biot–Savart law** — The field of a current element, dB = (µ₀/4π) I dl × r̂ / r²; integrated, it gives µ₀I/(2πr) for a long wire and µ₀I/(2R) at the center of a loop. *First defined in* [04-06](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-06-magnetic-fields-and-forces.md).

<a id="bisection-method"></a>**Bisection method** — Root finding by repeatedly halving a bracket that contains a sign change; after n steps the bracket width is (b − a)/2ⁿ, about 3.3 steps per decimal digit, and it cannot fail once a bracket is found. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md).

<a id="bit-error-rate-ber"></a>**Bit error rate (BER)** — The probability, or long-run fraction, that a transmitted bit is received in error; serial-link standards specify targets such as 1e-12. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="bit-field"></a>**Bit field** — A group of adjacent bits inside a register or word that holds one value (a 3-bit mode at bits 6:4); extracted with shift-and-mask and written by clearing the field and OR-ing in the shifted value. *First defined in* [05-07](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-07-bit-manipulation.md).

<a id="bit-mask"></a>**Bit mask** — A bit pattern with 1s at the positions of interest, used with AND to test or keep bits, OR to set them, AND-NOT to clear them and XOR to toggle them. *First defined in* [05-07](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-07-bit-manipulation.md).

<a id="blochs-theorem"></a>**Bloch's theorem** — In a periodic potential the electron eigenstates are plane waves times a function with the lattice period, ψ_k(x) = e^(ikx) u_k(x); such waves travel through a perfect crystal without scattering. *First defined in* [04-11](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-11-intro-solid-state-physics.md).

<a id="boolean-mask"></a>**Boolean mask** — An array of True/False values from an elementwise comparison, used to select elements (x[mask]) or count them (mask.sum()); combine masks with &, | and ~. *First defined in* [05-02](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-02-numpy-and-vectorization.md).

<a id="boundary-value-analysis"></a>**Boundary-value analysis** — Black-box test design that places tests just below, at and just above each boundary of the input ranges, where off-by-one errors (< versus <=) live. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md).

<a id="branch"></a>**Branch** — A single element, or a path through one element, connecting two nodes of a circuit. *First defined in* [06-01](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-01-charge-current-voltage-power.md).

<a id="brents-method"></a>**Brent's method** — A bracketing root-finder (SciPy's brentq) that combines bisection's guaranteed convergence with faster secant and inverse-quadratic steps; it never leaves the bracket and typically needs a few times fewer evaluations than bisection. *First defined in* [05-03](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-03-scipy-sympy-matplotlib.md). *See also:* [Root-finding](#root-finding), [Bisection method](#bisection-method).

<a id="broadcasting"></a>**Broadcasting** — NumPy's rule for combining arrays of different shapes; trailing axes must match or be 1, and size-1 axes are stretched without copying, so a column and a row combine into a full table. *First defined in* [05-02](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-02-numpy-and-vectorization.md).

<a id="buffer-overflow"></a>**Buffer overflow** — Reading or writing past the end (or before the start) of an array or buffer, corrupting or leaking neighboring memory; a leading cause of security vulnerabilities in C and C++. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md).

<a id="butterworth-response"></a>**Butterworth response** — The maximally flat filter response; a second-order Butterworth section has ζ = 0.707 (Q = 0.707), no peak, and −3.01 dB at its natural frequency. *First defined in* [02-04](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-04-forced-response-and-resonance.md).

<a id="letter-c"></a>

## C

<a id="c-string"></a>**C string** — An array of char terminated by a zero byte; it needs strlen + 1 bytes of storage, and functions find its end by scanning for the zero, so a missing terminator or a too-small buffer causes overflows. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md).

<a id="capacitance"></a>**Capacitance** — The charge a pair of conductors holds per volt of potential difference, C = Q/V (farads); it depends only on geometry and the insulator, e.g. ε A/d for parallel plates and 2πεℓ/ln(b/a) for a coax. *First defined in* [04-04](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-04-potential-capacitance-and-dielectrics.md).

<a id="capacitive-sensing"></a>**Capacitive sensing** — Detecting a finger or object by the change it makes in an electrode's capacitance; self-capacitance sensing sees a finger add C_F to the pad's parasitic C_P, mutual-capacitance sensing sees the transmit-receive coupling fall. *First defined in* [04-03](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-03-gauss-law.md).

<a id="catastrophic-cancellation"></a>**Catastrophic cancellation** — The loss of significant digits when subtracting two nearly equal floating-point numbers; avoided by algebraic rearrangement or series expansion. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="cauchy-distribution"></a>**Cauchy distribution** — The density 1/(π(1 + x²)), the ratio of two independent standard Gaussians; its tails are so heavy that it has no mean or variance, so the CLT does not apply and an average of Cauchy samples is still Cauchy. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="cauer-network"></a>**Cauer network** — An RC ladder model whose capacitors connect to a reference at each node, mirroring physical layers in series; unlike a Foster network it can be cascaded with models of further stages. *First defined in* [02-09](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-09-systems-of-odes-and-matrix-exponential.md).

<a id="cccs"></a>**CCCS** — Current-controlled current source, i = β i_x, with dimensionless current gain β; SPICE element F. The core of a bipolar transistor's small-signal model and of a current mirror. *First defined in* [06-06](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-06-dependent-sources.md). *See also:* [Dependent source](#dependent-source).

<a id="ccdf"></a>**CCDF** — Complementary cumulative distribution function, P(X > x) = 1 − F(x); for signals, the fraction of time the instantaneous power exceeds each level above average. *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md).

<a id="ccvs"></a>**CCVS** — Current-controlled voltage source, v = r i_x, with transresistance r in ohms; SPICE element H, controlled by the current through a named voltage source. *First defined in* [06-06](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-06-dependent-sources.md). *See also:* [Dependent source](#dependent-source).

<a id="central-difference"></a>**Central difference** — The numerical derivative (f(x + h) − f(x − h))/(2h), whose truncation error falls as h² rather than h. *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md).

<a id="central-limit-theorem"></a>**Central limit theorem** — The standardized sum of many independent terms with finite variance tends to a Gaussian, whatever their distribution; accurate near the center, unreliable far into the tails. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="centroid"></a>**Centroid** — The balance point of a region or distribution, its first moment divided by its area (or total weight); the mean of a density and the Elmore delay are centroids. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md). *See also:* [Elmore delay](#elmore-delay).

<a id="chain-rule"></a>**Chain rule** — (f(g(x)))' = f'(g(x))·g'(x); rates of nested quantities multiply, as in d/dt sin(ωt) = ω cos(ωt). *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md).

<a id="change-of-variables"></a>**Change of variables** — The rule f_Y(y) = Σ f_X(xᵢ)/|g′(xᵢ)| over the points xᵢ with g(xᵢ) = y, giving the density of Y = g(X); probability is conserved as the axis is stretched or compressed. *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md).

<a id="characteristic-equation"></a>**Characteristic equation** — The polynomial equation obtained by substituting y = e^{st} into a linear constant-coefficient ODE, such as s² + 2αs + ω₀² = 0; its roots set the decay rates and oscillation frequencies of every natural response. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="characteristic-impedance"></a>**Characteristic impedance** — Z0, the ratio of voltage to current for a single wave traveling along a transmission line (typically 50 Ω for coaxial cable and RF systems). For a lumped LC tank the analogous quantity is √(L/C), which sets the voltage swing per ampere of current step and the damping needed. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="characteristic-polynomial"></a>**Characteristic polynomial** — det(A − λI), a degree-n polynomial in λ whose roots are the eigenvalues; for 2×2 it is λ² − (trace)λ + det. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md). *See also:* [Characteristic equation](#characteristic-equation).

<a id="charge-density"></a>**Charge density** — Charge per unit length (λ, C/m), area (σ, C/m²) or volume (ρ, C/m³), used to integrate the fields of continuous distributions. *First defined in* [04-02](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-02-charge-coulomb-and-electric-fields.md).

<a id="charge-sharing"></a>**Charge sharing** — Connecting capacitors at different voltages so their charge redistributes to a common voltage; charge is conserved but energy is lost (half, for equal capacitors), and it is how a DRAM cell is read onto its bit line. *First defined in* [04-04](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-04-potential-capacitance-and-dielectrics.md).

<a id="charged-device-model-cdm"></a>**Charged-device model (CDM)** — The component ESD test of JS-002, modeling a charged device discharging quickly to ground through one pin; the industry-recommended target is 250 V, trending lower for high-speed parts. *First defined in* [04-02](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-02-charge-coulomb-and-electric-fields.md).

<a id="chebyshevs-inequality"></a>**Chebyshev's inequality** — P(|X − μ| ≥ kσ) ≤ 1/k² for any distribution with finite variance; a guarantee that is loose for any particular distribution (11.1% at 3σ against 0.27% for a Gaussian). *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md).

<a id="chi-square-distribution"></a>**Chi-square distribution** — The distribution of a sum of squared independent standard normals; with one degree of freedom it describes the instantaneous power of Gaussian noise, whose standard deviation is √2 times its mean. *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md).

<a id="chiplet"></a>**Chiplet** — A die designed to be combined with other dies inside one package, so that a system can exceed the reticle limit or mix processes; chiplets communicate over die-to-die links. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="chopper-stabilization"></a>**Chopper stabilization** — Modulating a low-frequency signal above an amplifier's 1/f corner, amplifying it there and demodulating it, which removes offset and 1/f noise at the cost of switching artifacts; the basis of zero-drift amplifiers. *First defined in* [03-06](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-06-random-processes-preview.md).

<a id="chromatic-dispersion"></a>**Chromatic dispersion** — The spreading of a light pulse because different wavelengths travel at different speeds; about 17 ps/(nm·km) at 1550 nm and near zero at 1310 nm in standard single-mode fiber. *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="co-packaged-optics"></a>**Co-packaged optics** — Optical engines placed in the same package as a switch or processor chip, shortening the electrical path to cut power per bit; announced by NVIDIA and Broadcom for 2025–2026 switches (as of Nov 2026). *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="coaxial-line"></a>**Coaxial line** — An inner conductor inside a coaxial outer conductor carrying equal and opposite charge; the field λ/(2πε₀r) is confined between them, strongest at the inner conductor, and zero outside. *First defined in* [04-03](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-03-gauss-law.md).

<a id="code-coverage"></a>**Code coverage** — The fraction of code exercised by tests, by statement, branch (decision) or MC/DC criteria; it shows what was not tested, not that what ran was checked. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md). *See also:* [MC/DC](#mc-dc).

<a id="code-review"></a>**Code review** — Examination of every change by another engineer before it is merged, catching defects tests miss, spreading knowledge and enforcing standards; the software counterpart of segregation of duties. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md).

<a id="cofactor"></a>**Cofactor** — C_ij = (−1)^(i+j) times the determinant of the matrix with row i and column j deleted; expanding along a row, det A = Σ a_ij C_ij. Practical only for small matrices. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md).

<a id="column-space"></a>**Column space** — C(A), the set of all combinations Ax of the columns of A; Ax = b is solvable exactly when b lies in it. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md).

<a id="commit"></a>**Commit** — In git, a permanent snapshot of the staged project plus its author, date, message and parent commit, named by a hash of its content; commits chain into the project's history. *First defined in* [05-04](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-04-reproducible-workflows.md).

<a id="common-impedance-coupling"></a>**Common-impedance coupling** — Interference between two circuits whose currents share a conductor; each circuit's current through the shared impedance produces a voltage in the other, as when a sensor and a motor share a ground return. *First defined in* [06-05](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-05-mesh-analysis.md). *See also:* [Star ground](#star-ground), [IR drop](#ir-drop).

<a id="common-mode-failure"></a>**Common-mode failure** — A failure that takes down several redundant units at once through a shared cause (power feed, design bug, environment), defeating redundancy. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="common-mode-rejection-ratio-cmrr"></a>**Common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR)** — The ratio of differential gain to common-mode gain, A_d/A_cm, usually in dB; for a difference amplifier built from resistors of tolerance t it is at worst about (1 + G)/(4t). *First defined in* [06-10](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-10-ideal-op-amp.md). *See also:* [Instrumentation amplifier](#instrumentation-amplifier).

<a id="companion-model"></a>**Companion model** — The conductance-plus-current-source equivalent that SPICE substitutes for a nonlinear device at each Newton iteration (its tangent line) or for a capacitor or inductor at each time step (its discretized law), so the circuit can be solved by linear MNA. *First defined in* [02-10](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-10-numerical-methods.md). *See also:* [Newton–Raphson method](#newton-raphson-method), [Modified nodal analysis](#modified-nodal-analysis).

<a id="compiler"></a>**Compiler** — A program that translates source code (C, for example) into machine instructions ahead of time, checking types and syntax; its output is assembly or object code for one processor architecture. *First defined in* [05-05](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-05-c-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Linker](#linker), [Preprocessor](#preprocessor), [Interpreter](#interpreter).

<a id="completing-the-square"></a>**Completing the square** — Rewriting x² + px + q as (x + p/2)² + (q − p²/4); it turns an irreducible quadratic into an arctangent integral, and in the Laplace domain into a damped sinusoid. *First defined in* [01-06](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-06-techniques-of-integration.md).

<a id="complex-conjugate"></a>**Complex conjugate** — For z = x + jy, the number z\* = x − jy, its mirror image across the real axis. z z\* = |z|², which is why conjugates are used to divide complex numbers. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="complex-exponential"></a>**Complex exponential** — A signal e^{st} with complex s = σ + jω. It rotates at ω rad/s while its magnitude grows (σ > 0), decays (σ < 0) or stays constant (σ = 0); its real part is a growing, decaying or steady sinusoid. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="complex-number"></a>**Complex number** — A number z = x + jy with real part x and imaginary part y (both real numbers), drawn as a point or arrow in the complex plane. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md). *See also:* [Imaginary unit](#imaginary-unit), [Complex plane](#complex-plane).

<a id="complex-plane"></a>**Complex plane** — The plane in which a complex number x + jy is plotted at horizontal coordinate x (real axis) and vertical coordinate y (imaginary axis). *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="complex-replacement"></a>**Complex replacement** — Solving an ODE with input cos ωt by solving it with input e^{jωt} and taking the real part; valid because the equation has real coefficients. It is the proof behind phasor analysis. *First defined in* [02-04](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-04-forced-response-and-resonance.md). *See also:* [Phasor](#phasor).

<a id="condition-number"></a>**Condition number** — κ = σ_max/σ_min for a square invertible matrix, the worst-case amplification of relative error when solving Ax = b; a large κ, not a small determinant, means nearly singular. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="conditional-distribution"></a>**Conditional distribution** — The distribution of Y given X = x, the joint distribution divided by the marginal of X along that slice. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="conditional-expectation"></a>**Conditional expectation** — E[Y | X = x], the mean of the conditional distribution of Y given X = x; evaluated at the random X, E[Y | X] is itself a random variable, the minimum mean-square-error predictor of Y, and E[E[Y | X]] = E[Y] (law of iterated expectations). *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="conditional-independence"></a>**Conditional independence** — Events that are independent once a third event (such as a die's true state) is known, even though they may be dependent unconditionally. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="conditional-probability"></a>**Conditional probability** — P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B), the probability of A among the outcomes where B occurred. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md). *See also:* [Bayes' rule](#bayes-rule).

<a id="conductance"></a>**Conductance** — The reciprocal of resistance, G = 1/R = i/v, in siemens (A/V); convenient for parallel elements and nodal analysis. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md). *See also:* [Resistance](#resistance).

<a id="conductance-matrix"></a>**Conductance matrix** — The matrix G of nodal analysis, G v = i. Diagonal entries are the total conductance at each node; off-diagonal entries are minus the conductance between two nodes. It is symmetric, sparse and, once a node is grounded, nonsingular. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md). *See also:* [Stamp](#stamp), [Modified nodal analysis](#modified-nodal-analysis).

<a id="confidence-interval"></a>**Confidence interval** — An interval computed from data by a procedure that covers the true parameter in a stated fraction (for example 95%) of repeated experiments; any single interval either contains the truth or not. *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="conjugate-match"></a>**Conjugate match** — The AC form of maximum power transfer, Z_L = Z_th\*, in which the load's resistance equals the source's and its reactance cancels the source's. *First defined in* [06-09](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-09-maximum-power-transfer.md). *See also:* [Matched load](#matched-load), [Maximum power transfer](#maximum-power-transfer).

<a id="conservative-field"></a>**Conservative field** — A vector field whose line integrals depend only on the endpoints, equivalently the gradient of a potential, equivalently curl-free on a region without holes; electrostatic fields are conservative, which is what makes voltage well defined. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md). *See also:* [Line integral](#line-integral), [Curl](#curl).

<a id="continuity"></a>**Continuity** — f is continuous at a if f(a) is defined, the limit at a exists, and the two are equal; informally, the graph can be drawn without lifting the pen. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md).

<a id="continuity-equation"></a>**Continuity equation** — Charge conservation in local form, ∇ · J = −∂ρ/∂t; integrated over a node that stores no charge it becomes Kirchhoff's current law. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="continuity-of-capacitor-voltage-and-inductor-current"></a>**Continuity of capacitor voltage and inductor current** — The rule that v_C and i_L cannot change instantaneously (it would take infinite current or voltage, and infinite power). Other circuit variables can jump at switching instants. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="continuous-integration"></a>**Continuous integration** — CI; automatically building and testing a project on a clean machine every time a change is pushed, so problems that depend on one person's setup are caught within minutes. *First defined in* [05-04](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-04-reproducible-workflows.md).

<a id="convolution"></a>**Convolution** — The operation y(t) = ∫ h(t−λ) u(λ) dλ that gives a linear time-invariant system's output from its input and impulse response; for a first-order low-pass, an exponentially weighted average of past inputs. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="corner-frequency"></a>**Corner frequency** — For a single-pole response H = 1/(1 + jωτ), the frequency ω = 1/τ where |H| = 1/√2 (−3 dB) and the phase is −45°; commonly used to define bandwidth. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="correlation-coefficient"></a>**Correlation coefficient** — ρ = Cov(X, Y)/(σ_X σ_Y), between −1 and 1; it measures only linear association, so uncorrelated variables can still be dependent. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="correlation-time"></a>**Correlation time** — The time scale τ_c over which a process's autocorrelation decays (RC for RC-filtered noise); a record of length T holds about T/(2τ_c) independent samples. *First defined in* [03-06](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-06-random-processes-preview.md).

<a id="coulomb-counting"></a>**Coulomb counting** — Estimating a battery's state of charge by integrating measured current over time; offsets accumulate, so gauges recalibrate at known states. *First defined in* [01-05](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-05-integrals.md).

<a id="coulombs-law"></a>**Coulomb's law** — The force between point charges, F = q₁q₂/(4πε₀r²) along the line joining them; repulsive for like signs, attractive for unlike, falling as the inverse square of distance. *First defined in* [04-02](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-02-charge-coulomb-and-electric-fields.md).

<a id="coupling-and-cohesion"></a>**Coupling and cohesion** — Coupling is how much modules depend on each other; cohesion is how focused a module is on one purpose. Good designs have low coupling (narrow, stable interfaces) and high cohesion. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md).

<a id="coupling-coefficient"></a>**Coupling coefficient** — k = M/√(L₁L₂), from 0 (no shared flux) to 1 (all flux shared); near 1 for windings on a common core, much lower for separated coils such as a wireless charger's. *First defined in* [04-07](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-07-faraday-lenz-and-inductance.md).

<a id="covariance"></a>**Covariance** — Cov(X, Y) = E[(X − μ_X)(Y − μ_Y)] = E[XY] − μ_Xμ_Y; zero for independent variables, and the cross term in the variance of a sum. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="cramers-rule"></a>**Cramer's rule** — For a nonsingular system, xᵢ = det(Bᵢ)/det(A), where Bᵢ is A with column i replaced by b. Useful for small symbolic results, never for large numerical systems. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md).

<a id="crest-factor"></a>**Crest factor** — Peak value divided by RMS value; √2 for a sine, 1 for a square wave, √3 for a triangle. Instruments and amplifiers specify the crest factor they can handle. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md).

<a id="critical-point"></a>**Critical point** — A point where f'(x) = 0 or f' does not exist; interior maxima and minima occur only at critical points (Fermat's theorem). *First defined in* [01-04](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-04-applications-of-derivatives.md).

<a id="critically-damped"></a>**Critically damped** — A second-order system with ζ = 1, whose repeated root gives the response (c₁ + c₂t)e^{−αt}; the boundary between ringing and creeping, though not the fastest to settle within a tolerance band. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="cross-product"></a>**Cross product** — a × b, a vector perpendicular to both a and b, of length |a||b|sin θ (the area of their parallelogram), directed by the right-hand rule. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md).

<a id="cryptographic-hash"></a>**Cryptographic hash** — A function (SHA-1, SHA-256) mapping any data to a fixed-length fingerprint such that any change to the input changes about half the output bits and collisions are infeasible to find; git names files and commits by such hashes. *First defined in* [05-04](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-04-reproducible-workflows.md).

<a id="crystal-lattice"></a>**Crystal lattice** — A periodic array of points in space at each of which an identical group of atoms (the basis) sits; silicon is a diamond lattice, two interpenetrating face-centered cubic lattices, with 8 atoms per cubic cell of side 0.5431 nm. *First defined in* [04-11](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-11-intro-solid-state-physics.md).

<a id="cumulative-distribution-function-cdf"></a>**Cumulative distribution function (CDF)** — F_X(x) = P(X ≤ x), which rises from 0 to 1; any interval probability is a difference of CDF values, and the density is its derivative. *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md).

<a id="curl"></a>**Curl** — ∇ × F, the circulation of a vector field per unit area at a point, as a vector along the axis of rotation; magnetic fields have curl where current flows. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md).

<a id="current-density"></a>**Current density** — Current per unit area as a vector field, J = nqv_d (A/m²); the current through a surface is the flux of J, and J = σE in an ohmic material. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="current-divider"></a>**Current divider** — Parallel resistors sharing a current in proportion to their conductances; for two, i1 = i R2/(R1 + R2), so the smaller resistor takes the larger current. *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md).

<a id="cyclomatic-complexity"></a>**Cyclomatic complexity** — McCabe's count of linearly independent paths through a function, M = E − N + 2 for its control-flow graph, equal to the number of decision points plus one; also the number of basis-path tests. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md).

<a id="cyclotron-frequency"></a>**Cyclotron frequency** — The orbital frequency of a charge in a uniform magnetic field, f_c = |q|B/(2πm), independent of speed; 28.0 GHz per tesla for an electron. *First defined in* [04-06](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-06-magnetic-fields-and-forces.md).

<a id="letter-d"></a>

## D

<a id="damped-natural-frequency"></a>**Damped natural frequency** — ω_d = ω₀√(1 − ζ²), the frequency at which an underdamped system actually rings. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md). *See also:* [Natural frequency](#natural-frequency).

<a id="damping-ratio"></a>**Damping ratio** — ζ = α/ω₀, the single number that classifies a second-order system: underdamped (ζ < 1, rings), critically damped (ζ = 1) or overdamped (ζ > 1); overshoot depends only on ζ. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="dbm"></a>**dBm** — Power expressed in decibels relative to 1 mW, 10·log10(P / 1 mW); 0 dBm = 1 mW and 30 dBm = 1 W. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md). *See also:* [Decibel](#decibel).

<a id="dc-gain"></a>**DC gain** — H(0), the steady-state output per unit of constant input for a stable system; it is also the final value of the unit-step response. *First defined in* [02-05](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-05-laplace-transform-for-odes.md). *See also:* [Transfer function](#transfer-function), [Final-value theorem](#final-value-theorem).

<a id="de-broglie-wavelength"></a>**De Broglie wavelength** — The wavelength λ = h/p associated with a particle of momentum p; about 0.12 nm for a 100 eV electron, comparable to atomic spacings, which is why electrons diffract from crystals. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="de-moivres-theorem"></a>**De Moivre's theorem** — (r∠θ)ⁿ = rⁿ∠nθ. Raising a complex number to a power raises its magnitude to that power and multiplies its angle. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="decibel"></a>**Decibel** — A logarithmic ratio, 10·log10 of a power ratio (or 20·log10 of an amplitude ratio for equal impedances); 3 dB ≈ 2× power, 10 dB = 10× power. *First defined in* [00-01](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-01-map-of-electrical-engineering.md).

<a id="decision-feedback-equalizer-dfe"></a>**Decision-feedback equalizer (DFE)** — A receiver equalizer that subtracts the interference of earlier symbols computed from its own past decisions; one wrong decision can then cause a burst of errors, which transmitter precoding limits to about two bit errors. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="defect-level-dppm"></a>**Defect level (DPPM)** — The fraction of shipped (test-passing) parts that are defective, usually in defective parts per million; the Williams–Brown model gives DL = 1 − Y^(1−T). *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="defective-matrix"></a>**Defective matrix** — A square matrix with fewer independent eigenvectors than its size (a repeated eigenvalue short of eigenvectors); it cannot be diagonalized, and its powers and exponentials contain extra factors k or t. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="definite-integral"></a>**Definite integral** — The limit of Riemann sums ∫_a^b f(x) dx, equal to the signed area under f; its units are those of f times those of x. *First defined in* [01-05](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-05-integrals.md).

<a id="delta-wye-transformation"></a>**Delta–wye transformation** — Replacing three resistors in a triangle (delta) by three meeting at a node (wye), or the reverse, with equal behaviour at the three terminals; R_a = R_ab R_ca/(R_ab + R_bc + R_ca). *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md).

<a id="density-of-states"></a>**Density of states** — The number of electron states per unit energy (and per unit volume), g(E) ∝ √E for free electrons; multiplied by the occupation f(E) it gives how many electrons sit at each energy. *First defined in* [04-11](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-11-intro-solid-state-physics.md).

<a id="dependent-source"></a>**Dependent source** — An ideal voltage or current source whose value is a fixed multiple of a voltage or current elsewhere in the circuit (VCVS, VCCS, CCVS, CCCS); it models gain in transistors and amplifiers and stays in place when independent sources are turned off. *First defined in* [06-06](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-06-dependent-sources.md). *See also:* [VCVS](#vcvs), [VCCS](#vccs), [CCVS](#ccvs), [CCCS](#cccs), [Small-signal model](#small-signal-model).

<a id="depletion-region"></a>**Depletion region** — The layer around a pn junction stripped of mobile carriers, leaving fixed ionized dopants (−qN_A on the p side, +qN_D on the n side); Gauss's law gives its triangular field, peaking at the junction. *First defined in* [04-03](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-03-gauss-law.md).

<a id="dereference"></a>**Dereference** — To access the object a pointer points to (\*p in C, or p->field for a struct); dereferencing an invalid or null pointer is undefined behavior. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md).

<a id="derivative"></a>**Derivative** — The instantaneous rate of change f'(a) = lim_{h→0} (f(a + h) − f(a))/h, the slope of the tangent line; its units are the output's units per input unit. *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md). *See also:* [Difference quotient](#difference-quotient), [Differentiable](#differentiable).

<a id="design-for-test-dft"></a>**Design for test (DFT)** — Design features (scan chains, built-in self-test, test access) that make manufactured chips testable for defects at low cost. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="design-verification"></a>**Design verification** — The engineering function (and activity) of demonstrating, before tapeout, that a design's RTL implements its specification, using simulation, coverage, formal methods and emulation. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="determinant"></a>**Determinant** — The number det A attached to a square matrix, fixed by three rules (det I = 1, a row exchange flips the sign, linearity in each row); it equals ± the product of the pivots, is zero exactly when A is singular, and |det A| is the volume scale factor of the map x → Ax. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md). *See also:* [Cofactor](#cofactor), [Inverse matrix](#inverse-matrix).

<a id="diagonalization"></a>**Diagonalization** — Writing A = XΛX⁻¹ with eigenvectors in X and eigenvalues in Λ, possible when A has n independent eigenvectors; it gives powers as Aᵏ = XΛᵏX⁻¹. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="diagonally-dominant-matrix"></a>**Diagonally dominant matrix** — A matrix in which each diagonal entry is at least the sum of the magnitudes of the other entries in its row; a nodal conductance matrix is, with strict inequality at nodes that have conductance to ground. *First defined in* [06-04](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-04-nodal-analysis.md). *See also:* [Conductance matrix](#conductance-matrix), [Positive definite matrix](#positive-definite-matrix).

<a id="dielectric"></a>**Dielectric** — An insulator that polarizes in an electric field, reducing the field of a given free charge by its relative permittivity ε_r and raising a capacitor's capacitance by the same factor. *First defined in* [04-04](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-04-potential-capacitance-and-dielectrics.md). *See also:* [Relative permittivity](#relative-permittivity).

<a id="dielectric-breakdown"></a>**Dielectric breakdown** — The sudden failure of an insulator when the field is strong enough to tear electrons loose and start an avalanche; about 3 MV/m in air and above 10 MV/cm in thermal SiO₂. *First defined in* [04-02](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-02-charge-coulomb-and-electric-fields.md).

<a id="dies-per-wafer"></a>**Dies per wafer** — The number of whole dies that fit on a round wafer, approximated by πd²/(4A) − πd/√(2A); the subtracted edge-loss term grows in relative size as dies get larger. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md).

<a id="difference-quotient"></a>**Difference quotient** — The slope (f(a + h) − f(a))/h of the secant line through two nearby points; its limit as h → 0 is the derivative. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md).

<a id="differentiable"></a>**Differentiable** — Having a derivative at a point; differentiability implies continuity, but not conversely (|x| is continuous with a corner at 0). *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md).

<a id="differential-nonlinearity-dnl"></a>**Differential nonlinearity (DNL)** — For a data converter, the deviation of each code step from the ideal 1 LSB, in LSBs; it is largest where many bits switch at once, such as the major carry. *First defined in* [06-07](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-07-linearity-and-superposition.md). *See also:* [Superposition](#superposition).

<a id="differential-signaling"></a>**Differential signaling** — Sending a signal as equal and opposite voltages on two wires and receiving their difference, which doubles the signal and cancels interference common to both wires. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="diffraction"></a>**Diffraction** — The spreading of a wave through an aperture or around an edge by about λ/aperture radians; a slit's first zero is at sin θ = λ/a, a circular aperture's at 1.22λ/D. *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="dimension"></a>**Dimension** — The number of vectors in any basis of a subspace (all bases have the same number). *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md).

<a id="dimensional-analysis"></a>**Dimensional analysis** — Checking that every term of an equation has the same physical units (and that arguments of exp, log and trig functions are dimensionless) to catch errors and derive relationships. *First defined in* [00-03](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-03-how-to-study-this-curriculum.md).

<a id="direct-band-gap"></a>**Direct band gap** — A band gap whose conduction-band minimum lies at the same crystal momentum as the valence-band maximum (GaAs, GaN), so electrons and holes recombine by emitting light efficiently; indirect gaps (Si, Ge, SiC) need a phonon. *First defined in* [04-11](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-11-intro-solid-state-physics.md).

<a id="direction-field"></a>**Direction field** — A plot of short segments with slope f(t, y) at a grid of points for y' = f(t, y); solutions run tangent to the segments, so the field shows their behavior before any algebra. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="directional-derivative"></a>**Directional derivative** — The rate of change of f along a unit vector u, D_u f = ∇f · u. *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="discount-factor"></a>**Discount factor** — D(t) = exp(−∫ r dt), the present value of one unit due at time t; it is exactly the integrating factor of the balance equation B' − r(t)B = deposits. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md). *See also:* [Integrating factor](#integrating-factor).

<a id="displacement-current"></a>**Displacement current** — The term ε₀ dΦ_E/dt that Maxwell added to Ampère's law; a changing electric field makes a magnetic field as a current does, so a charging capacitor's gap carries a displacement current equal to its lead current. *First defined in* [04-08](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-08-maxwell-preview.md).

<a id="distributed-rc-line"></a>**Distributed RC line** — A wire whose resistance and capacitance are spread along its length; driven by a step, its far end reaches 50% at about 0.38 RC, so delay grows as length squared. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="dither"></a>**Dither** — A small random signal added before a quantizer so that the quantization error stops tracking the signal. Triangular-PDF dither two steps wide makes the mean and power of the total error independent of the input, at the cost of tripling the error power. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="divergence"></a>**Divergence** — ∇ · F, the net outflow of a vector field per unit volume at a point; a source density. Gauss's law states ∇ · E = ρ/ε₀. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md). *See also:* [Flux](#flux).

<a id="divergence-theorem"></a>**Divergence theorem** — The total outward flux of a field through a closed surface equals the integral of its divergence over the enclosed volume; it turns local source density into a global balance. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md). *See also:* [Divergence](#divergence), [Flux](#flux).

<a id="domain-and-range"></a>**Domain and range** — The domain is the set of allowed inputs of a function; the range is the set of outputs it can produce. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md).

<a id="dot-product"></a>**Dot product** — a·b = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃ = |a||b|cos θ; it measures how far two vectors point the same way and is zero for perpendicular vectors. *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="double-integral"></a>**Double integral** — The integral of a function over a two-dimensional region, ∬ f dA; it sums a density (power per area, charge per area) over the region to give a total. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md).

<a id="drift-velocity"></a>**Drift velocity** — The small average velocity carriers acquire from a field on top of their fast random motion; about 74 µm/s for 1 A in 1 mm² of copper. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="driving-point-resistance"></a>**Driving-point resistance** — The resistance seen looking into a node with respect to ground, equal to the diagonal entry R_jj of the resistance matrix G⁻¹; the voltage at node j per ampere injected there. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md). *See also:* [Thevenin resistance](#thevenin-resistance).

<a id="drude-model"></a>**Drude model** — The classical picture of conduction in which carriers accelerate in a field and lose their momentum in random collisions every τ on average, giving σ = ne²τ/m and Ohm's law. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="dtype"></a>**dtype** — The single element type of a NumPy array (int8, uint8, int64, float32, float64, complex128, bool), fixing its range, precision and memory use. *First defined in* [05-02](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-02-numpy-and-vectorization.md).

<a id="dual-circuit"></a>**Dual circuit** — The circuit obtained from a planar one by turning meshes into nodes, resistances into equal-valued conductances, voltage sources into current sources and series into parallel; its node voltages equal the original's mesh currents. *First defined in* [06-05](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-05-mesh-analysis.md). *See also:* [Mesh analysis](#mesh-analysis), [Nodal analysis](#nodal-analysis).

<a id="dual-dirac-model"></a>**Dual-Dirac model** — A model of jitter as two spikes DJ(δδ) apart blurred by Gaussian random jitter of rms σ, giving total jitter TJ(BER) = DJ(δδ) + 2·Q_BER·σ, where the industry convention defines Q(Q_BER) = BER (2Q_BER = 14.069 at 1e-12; the literal model gives 13.68). *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md).

<a id="dual-slope-adc"></a>**Dual-slope ADC** — An integrating converter that integrates the input for a fixed time and times the de-integration with a reference; its result is independent of R and C, and integrating over whole mains periods rejects hum. *First defined in* [01-05](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-05-integrals.md).

<a id="duty-cycle"></a>**Duty cycle** — The fraction of time a block or signal is active; a block drawing current I for duty cycle D contributes D·I to the average current. *First defined in* [06-01](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-01-charge-current-voltage-power.md).

<a id="dynamic-power"></a>**Dynamic power** — Power consumed by charging and discharging capacitances in switching circuits, P = αCV²f, independent of the resistance of the charging path. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md). *See also:* [Activity factor](#activity-factor).

<a id="dynamic-typing"></a>**Dynamic typing** — Types belong to objects, not to names, so a name can refer to values of different types over time; checked at run time (type hints document intent but do not enforce it). *First defined in* [05-01](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-01-python-fundamentals.md).

<a id="dynamic-voltage-and-frequency-scaling-dvfs"></a>**Dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS)** — Lowering supply voltage and clock frequency together when full performance is not needed; because dynamic power scales roughly as V²f, power falls roughly as the cube of voltage. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md).

<a id="letter-e"></a>

## E

<a id="e-series-preferred-values"></a>**E-series (preferred values)** — The IEC 60063 series of standard component values with n values per decade spaced by about 10^(1/n), such as E12, E24 and E96, chosen so neighbouring values' tolerance bands roughly touch. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md). *See also:* [Tolerance](#tolerance).

<a id="eddy-currents"></a>**Eddy currents** — Currents induced in bulk conductors by changing magnetic flux; they cause braking, heating and core loss, which laminated and ferrite cores reduce. *First defined in* [04-07](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-07-faraday-lenz-and-inductance.md).

<a id="effective-mass"></a>**Effective mass** — The mass m\* = ħ²/(d²E/dk²) with which an electron in a band responds to external forces, set by the band's curvature; light effective masses mean high mobility. *First defined in* [04-11](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-11-intro-solid-state-physics.md).

<a id="effective-number-of-bits-enob"></a>**Effective number of bits (ENOB)** — (SINAD − 1.76)/6.02, the resolution of an ideal ADC with the same measured signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio as a real one. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md).

<a id="efficiency"></a>**Efficiency** — The ratio of output power to input power, η = P_out/P_in, of a converter or distribution path; efficiencies of stages in series multiply. *First defined in* [06-01](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-01-charge-current-voltage-power.md).

<a id="eigenvalue"></a>**Eigenvalue** — A number λ for which Ax = λx has a nonzero solution x; the roots of det(A − λI) = 0. They sum to the trace and multiply to the determinant. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md). *See also:* [Eigenvector](#eigenvector), [Characteristic polynomial](#characteristic-polynomial).

<a id="eigenvector"></a>**Eigenvector** — A nonzero vector x that a matrix only scales, Ax = λx; any nonzero multiple is also an eigenvector. In eigenvector coordinates a diagonalizable matrix acts as independent scalings. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="elasticity-sensitivity"></a>**Elasticity (sensitivity)** — The dimensionless ratio of relative changes, S = d ln y / d ln x = (x/y)(dy/dx); for y = kxⁿ it equals n. Engineers call it sensitivity, economists elasticity. *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md).

<a id="electric-charge"></a>**Electric charge** — The property that makes matter feel electric forces; it comes in two signs, is conserved, and is quantized in multiples of the elementary charge. Measured in coulombs (1 C = 1 A·s). *First defined in* [04-02](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-02-charge-coulomb-and-electric-fields.md).

<a id="electric-current"></a>**Electric current** — The rate at which charge crosses a surface, I = dQ/dt (amperes); conventional current points the way positive charge would move, opposite to electron motion in a metal. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="electric-dipole"></a>**Electric dipole** — Charges ±q a distance d apart, with dipole moment p = qd pointing from − to +; its far field falls as 1/r³, and in a uniform field it feels torque pE sin θ but no net force. *First defined in* [04-02](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-02-charge-coulomb-and-electric-fields.md).

<a id="electric-displacement"></a>**Electric displacement** — The field D = ε₀E + P = εE (C/m²), whose flux through a closed surface equals the enclosed free charge; its normal component is continuous across a boundary without free charge. *First defined in* [04-04](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-04-potential-capacitance-and-dielectrics.md).

<a id="electric-energy-density"></a>**Electric energy density** — The energy stored per unit volume in an electric field, u = ½εE² (J/m³); integrated over space it equals a capacitor's ½CV², and in a vacuum gap it equals the electrostatic pressure on the conductors. *First defined in* [04-04](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-04-potential-capacitance-and-dielectrics.md).

<a id="electric-field"></a>**Electric field** — The force per unit charge a small test charge would feel at a point, E = F/q (V/m); a point charge's field is q/(4πε₀r²) pointing away from a positive charge. *First defined in* [04-02](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-02-charge-coulomb-and-electric-fields.md).

<a id="electric-flux"></a>**Electric flux** — The surface integral of the electric field's normal component, Φ = ∬ E · n̂ dA (V·m); it counts field lines crossing a surface, and through a closed surface it equals the enclosed charge over ε₀. *First defined in* [04-03](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-03-gauss-law.md). *See also:* [Flux](#flux), [Gauss's law](#gausss-law).

<a id="electric-potential"></a>**Electric potential** — Potential energy per unit charge, V = U/q (volts, J/C), defined because the electrostatic field is conservative; V_b − V_a = −∫ E · dl, a point charge gives k_e q/r, and potentials add as scalars. *First defined in* [04-04](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-04-potential-capacitance-and-dielectrics.md). *See also:* [Conservative field](#conservative-field), [Equipotential](#equipotential).

<a id="electric-power"></a>**Electric power** — The rate of energy transfer, p = dw/dt = vi, in watts (1 W = 1 J/s = 1 V·A). *First defined in* [06-01](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-01-charge-current-voltage-power.md). *See also:* [Passive sign convention](#passive-sign-convention), [Average power](#average-power).

<a id="electrical-engineering"></a>**Electrical engineering** — The discipline of using electricity and electromagnetism to move and convert energy and to sense, move, store and process information. *First defined in* [00-01](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-01-map-of-electrical-engineering.md).

<a id="electromagnetic-wave"></a>**Electromagnetic wave** — Self-sustaining oscillating E and B fields, perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel, with E = cB; speed c/√ε_r in a dielectric. Radio, light and board signals are all such waves. *First defined in* [04-08](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-08-maxwell-preview.md).

<a id="electromigration"></a>**Electromigration** — The slow drift of metal atoms pushed by the electron current at high current density, forming voids and hillocks; it caps the DC current density in on-chip wires, especially power grids. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="electron-volt"></a>**Electron-volt** — The energy an electron gains (or the work done on it) crossing 1 V, exactly 1.602176634×10⁻¹⁹ J since 2019; the natural unit for band gaps, photon energies and per-electron energies. Also written electronvolt. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md).

<a id="electronic-design-automation-eda"></a>**Electronic design automation (EDA)** — The software used to design and verify chips and boards, covering simulation, synthesis, place-and-route, timing and verification; dominated commercially by Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens EDA. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="electrostatic-discharge-esd"></a>**Electrostatic discharge (ESD)** — The sudden flow of charge between objects at different potentials, typically a spark from a charged person or device; ICs are protected on-chip and qualified against standard ESD models. *First defined in* [04-02](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-02-charge-coulomb-and-electric-fields.md).

<a id="electrostatic-equilibrium"></a>**Electrostatic equilibrium** — The state of a conductor whose free charges have stopped moving; the field inside the metal is zero, net charge sits on the surface, and the field just outside is perpendicular with magnitude σ/ε₀. *First defined in* [04-03](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-03-gauss-law.md).

<a id="element-law"></a>**Element law** — The relation between an element's terminal voltage and current (its constitutive relation), such as v = Ri; with KCL and KVL it determines every voltage and current in a circuit. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md). *See also:* [i–v characteristic](#i-v-characteristic).

<a id="elementary-charge"></a>**Elementary charge** — The charge of a proton, e = 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C exactly (an electron carries −e); one coulomb is 6.242 × 10¹⁸ elementary charges. *First defined in* [04-02](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-02-charge-coulomb-and-electric-fields.md).

<a id="elmore-delay"></a>**Elmore delay** — The first moment (time centroid) of a network's impulse response, computed directly from its resistances and capacitances; a fast, somewhat pessimistic interconnect delay estimate. *First defined in* [01-06](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-06-techniques-of-integration.md).

<a id="emulation"></a>**Emulation** — Running a chip design on specialized hardware (emulators or FPGA prototypes) thousands to millions of times faster than simulation, so software can run before tapeout. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="endianness"></a>**Endianness** — The order of a multi-byte value's bytes in memory or on a wire; little-endian stores the least significant byte first (x86, most Arm MCUs), big-endian the most significant first (network byte order). *First defined in* [05-07](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-07-bit-manipulation.md).

<a id="energy-band"></a>**Energy band** — A range of closely spaced allowed electron energies in a crystal, formed when each atomic level of N coupled atoms splits into N levels; each band holds two electrons per primitive cell. *First defined in* [04-11](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-11-intro-solid-state-physics.md).

<a id="energy-per-bit"></a>**Energy per bit** — The energy (typically pJ/bit) consumed to move, store or process one bit; power = energy per bit × data rate. A key efficiency metric for links, memories and accelerators. *First defined in* [00-01](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-01-map-of-electrical-engineering.md).

<a id="engineering-change-order-eco"></a>**Engineering change order (ECO)** — A late design change made with minimal disruption, often by rewiring spare gates through metal-layer changes only. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="equilibrium-solution"></a>**Equilibrium solution** — A constant solution y\* of an autonomous equation y' = f(y), where f(y\*) = 0; it is stable if f'(y\*) < 0, with local time constant −1/f'(y\*), and unstable if f'(y\*) > 0. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="equipotential"></a>**Equipotential** — A surface (or line) of constant potential; moving along it takes no work, field lines cross it at right angles, and every conductor in equilibrium is one. *First defined in* [04-04](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-04-potential-capacitance-and-dielectrics.md).

<a id="equivalent-noise-bandwidth-enbw"></a>**Equivalent noise bandwidth (ENBW)** — The width of an ideal brick-wall filter passing the same white-noise power as a real filter, ∫₀^∞ |H(f)|² df divided by the passband gain; (π/2) f_c for one pole. *First defined in* [01-06](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-06-techniques-of-integration.md).

<a id="equivalent-oxide-thickness-eot"></a>**Equivalent oxide thickness (EOT)** — The SiO₂ thickness giving the same capacitance per area as a gate stack, EOT = Σ t_i × 3.9/ε_r,i; a 2 nm HfO₂ layer (ε_r = 25) counts as 0.312 nm. *First defined in* [04-04](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-04-potential-capacitance-and-dielectrics.md).

<a id="equivalent-resistance"></a>**Equivalent resistance** — The single resistance that has the same voltage–current relation at a pair of terminals as a network of resistors; it says nothing about the network's internal currents. *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md).

<a id="ergodicity"></a>**Ergodicity** — The property that time averages along one sample function converge to ensemble averages; it licenses measuring a process with one long recording. Unit-to-unit offsets are not ergodic. *First defined in* [03-06](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-06-random-processes-preview.md).

<a id="error-budget"></a>**Error budget** — A table of every error source's contribution to a system's output (each source times its gain to the output), combined by worst case or by root-sum-square. *First defined in* [06-07](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-07-linearity-and-superposition.md). *See also:* [Root-sum-square (RSS)](#root-sum-square-rss), [Worst-case analysis](#worst-case-analysis).

<a id="error-log"></a>**Error log** — A running record of every mistake, its cause and the rule that prevents it, used to target review and to avoid repeating errors. *First defined in* [00-03](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-03-how-to-study-this-curriculum.md).

<a id="error-vector-magnitude"></a>**Error vector magnitude** — EVM, the RMS distance between transmitted (or received) constellation points and their ideal positions, relative to the signal, often quoted in dB.
